newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises equity in Hebrosbank to 98 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises equity in Hebrosbank to 98 pct.

text.p: Bulgaria's Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) stake in Hebrosbank rose to 97.56 percent from 66.7 percent after private shareholders declined to subscribe to a rights issue, a BCC official said.
"Only the bank holding subscribed shares of the new issue, which brought state equity in Hebrosbank to 97.56 percent," said the official, who declined to be named.

An extraordinary shareholders' meeting of the Plovdiv-based bank decided on Tuesday to cut its capital from 15.26 billion levs to 10.4 billion levs after some 4.8 billion levs of the rights issue remained unsubscribed.

The BCC, which manages state equity in nine commercial banks, covered its contribution to Hebrosbank's capital rise through dollar-denominated domestic bad loan bonds worth $51 million, received under a government decision in June.
In July Hebrosbank decided to raise capital from 763 million levs to 15.3 billion levs through a rights issue open for subscription by October 6.

Among the biggest bank's private shareholders with some 32 percent equity before the rise are firms linked to private Trade & Savings Bank and Elitbank, which were put under special supervision by the central bank on September 23. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
